en: Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Mahwah, Bergen County, New Jersey, July 1925, Sheet 5

sheet-1-1.description: The lower half of sheet 1, below the key map, title and index, is a map at 100 ft to an inch of the south-west part of Mahwah village with north at the top. Maple Avenue runs down the left side from 3rd Street, which is cut by the heavy line under the key map, to Ramapo Avenue, which crosses the part diagonally to Island Road. Island Road runs down the middle of the sheet, and from it a second Ramapo Avenue runs east along the bottom past an unnamed street (lettered 'Not Named') to Winters Brook and a pond at the lower right. The land is in large, mostly vacant tracts with a few lots subdivided along Maple Avenue and Ramapo Avenue. Named buildings are the Mahwah Dutch Reformed Church (furnace heat, electric light) with its Sunday school rooms on Ramapo Avenue west of Island Road, and Mahwah Public School No. 1 (steam heat, electric light) on the east side of Island Road above Ramapo Avenue. Frame dwellings and garages are scattered along the roads. A boxed inset at the right, above the compass rose, shows Ramapo Avenue and Railroad Avenue west of the Erie Railroad and is georeferenced separately. The top of the part continues on sheet 3 and the inset area on sheet 2.
notes: The diagonal Ramapo Avenue west of Island Road is now West Ramapo Avenue; the Ramapo Avenue east of Island Road is now East Ramapo Avenue.
The street lettered 'Not Named' is now Devine Drive.
Maple Avenue at 3rd Street is the line of today's Avenue B; the junction was hand-picked from the drawn edges, about 15 ft beyond the heavy line under the key map.
Only five control points; the fit has 1.2 m RMSE but a large leave-one-out error.
Mahwah Dutch Reformed Church and Mahwah Public School No. 1.

Title sheet: key map of the township at 1500 ft to an inch, fire department notes and street index in the upper half (left out of the mask). Lower half is a map at 100 ft: part 1 (main map) from Maple Av and 3rd St to Island Rd and Ramapo Av (W. and E. Ramapo Av today), the street 'Not Named' (now Devine Drive), Winters Brook, Mahwah Dutch Reformed Church, Mahwah Public School No. 1; part 2 is the boxed inset at the right, Ramapo Av and Railroad Av west of the Erie R.R. with Winters Brook and a pond, also drawn on sheet 2, placed by points carried from sheet 2. Two parts.

sheet-1-2.description: A boxed inset at the right of sheet 1, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with its own compass rose, showing the area just west of the Erie Railroad station where Ramapo Avenue meets Railroad Avenue. Ramapo Avenue runs east from Winters Brook to Railroad Avenue, and a second Ramapo Avenue branches south-east from it to Railroad Avenue lower down; Railroad Avenue runs along the right edge of the inset, with only its west side drawn. North of Ramapo Avenue is a property with a large frame building, wagon sheds, storage buildings and a dwelling; south of it Winters Brook widens into a pond, beside which stand an ice house and two dwellings. The figures 2 printed around the inset show that the same ground is drawn on sheet 2, at its left edge.
notes: Placed by four points carried from sheet 2 (street corners and a dwelling corner drawn on both sheets); low confidence, and the left half of the inset (the brook and pond) has no control of its own.
The road layout at the junction has changed: today's Old Station Lane, Ramapo Avenue and North and South Railroad Avenue did not fit the drawn junctions consistently, so no modern junction is used.
Ice house beside the pond on Winters Brook.

Title sheet: key map of the township at 1500 ft to an inch, fire department notes and street index in the upper half (left out of the mask). Lower half is a map at 100 ft: part 1 (main map) from Maple Av and 3rd St to Island Rd and Ramapo Av (W. and E. Ramapo Av today), the street 'Not Named' (now Devine Drive), Winters Brook, Mahwah Dutch Reformed Church, Mahwah Public School No. 1; part 2 is the boxed inset at the right, Ramapo Av and Railroad Av west of the Erie R.R. with Winters Brook and a pond, also drawn on sheet 2, placed by points carried from sheet 2. Two parts.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the business centre of Mahwah east of the Erie Railroad, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with north at the top. The Erie Railroad main line runs down the left side of the sheet between Railroad Avenue on its west side and a second Railroad Avenue on its east side; beyond the western Railroad Avenue a strip of dwellings and a pond are shown. Franklin Turnpike runs diagonally from the top centre to King Street (Franklin Lane) at the bottom, and Miller Road crosses the sheet from Franklin Turnpike eastward. North of Miller Road are Winter Place, Winter Terrace, Babcock Road, Tatham Road, Hillside Avenue, Winter (Wausau) Avenue and Olney Road, laid out as a grid of small residential lots, many of them still vacant. The North Jersey Rapid Transit Company's electric right of way runs north and south between Franklin Turnpike and Hillside Avenue. Around the railroad and Ramapo Avenue are the village's commercial buildings: the Ramapo Hotel, a club with the post office in a brick store block, the Erie passenger station, freight house, a coal pocket with its conveyor, hay and grain warehouses, a garage on Franklin Turnpike, and the Honey Bottling works near King Street. A small park lies on the north side of Ramapo Avenue east of the tracks. Galli's Inn stands on the east side of the tracks near the top of the sheet and the Mahwah Inn in large grounds east of Olney Road. South of Miller Road only the street openings of Oweno Road and Malcolm Road and a stretch of Hillside Avenue are drawn; the rest of that area is shown on sheet 5. Most buildings are frame dwellings with a few in brick and stone.
notes: Tatham Road is now Lawrence Road.
Winter (Wausau) Avenue is now Winter Street.
King (Franklin Lane) is now King Street.
Hillside Avenue jogs at Miller Road: North Hillside Avenue to the north, Hillside Avenue to the south.
The junction of Ramapo Avenue and the western Railroad Avenue was rejected (8.9 m off the fit); the road layout by the station has changed.
North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. electric right of way drawn between Franklin Turnpike and Hillside Avenue.

Village east of the Erie R.R. at 100 ft: Railroad Av (west of the tracks), Franklin Turnpike, Winter Pl, Winter Ter, Babcock Rd, Olney Rd, Tatham Rd (now Lawrence Road), Hillside Av, Winter (Wausau) Av (now Winter Street), Miller Rd, Ramapo Av, King (Franklin Lane) (now King Street); North Jersey Rapid Transit Co. right of way; Galli's Inn, Ramapo Hotel, Mahwah Inn, post office. One part.

sheet-3-1.description: The main part of sheet 3 shows the western end of Mahwah village between the New York state line and Island Road, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with north at the top. A heavy line along the state line divides it from the turned Suffern part at the left. Ramapo Valley Road crosses the part diagonally from the lower left to the top right, where it meets Reich Avenue and Island Road beside the Ramapo River. North-west of it a grid of narrow numbered lots lies along Franklin Avenue, Hines, 1st Street and a short 2nd Street, with scattered frame dwellings. South-east of the road the streets run towards Island Road: Wilmuth and Abelone, both marked as arbitrary names, Warhol, Sherwood Avenue, and further south 1st, 2nd and 3rd Streets crossed by Avenue A, Avenue B and Maple Avenue. Most of these blocks are subdivided into long rows of small lots, many still vacant, with frame dwellings and private garages clustered near Ramapo Valley Road and Island Road. Named buildings are the First Zion Church of Mahwah near Island Road and a dance hall in the block north of Warhol and another on Wilmuth. Island Road along the right edge is drawn with its west side only near the bottom; the land beyond is on sheet 4. The lower right corner is a block of large lots fronting Island Road, and the bottom edge continues on sheet 1. The sheet carries its own compass rose and a 100 ft scale bar.
notes: The 1st Street north of Ramapo Valley Road is now Strysko Avenue; the 2nd Street by Hines is now South Street; Franklin Avenue is now Franklin Place; Hines is Hines Avenue.
The 1st Street between Avenue A and Avenue B is now Church Street; it is drawn ending short of Island Road, where lots front the road.
Abelone (arbitrary) and its continuation to Island Road follow the line of today's Sherwood Avenue; its junctions with Ramapo Valley Road and Island Road lay 14 to 16 m off the fit and were rejected.
The street lettered Sherwood Avenue on the sheet is on the line of today's Grove Street.
Maple Avenue is the continuation of Avenue B south of 3rd Street.
First Zion Church of Mahwah, heated by stove, lit by electricity.
An earlier configuration matched the wrong drawn streets to Sherwood Avenue, Grove Street and Church Street (7.5 m RMSE); it was re-seeded from full-resolution crops.

West village and the New York side at 100 ft. Part 1 (main, north up), right of the heavy line along the state line: Ramapo Valley Rd, Reich Av, 1st St (now Strysko Av), Franklin Av (now Franklin Pl), Hines, 2nd St (now South St), Wilmuth, Abelone (on the line of today's Sherwood Av), Warhol, Sherwood Av (on the line of today's Grove St), Island Rd, Avenue A, Avenue B, 1st St (now Church St), 2nd, 3rd Sts, Maple Av; First Zion Church. Part 2, left of the line, turned with north to the right: Village of Suffern, N.Y. ('This territory also shown on Suffern survey'): State, 1st St, Jersey Av, Brook Av (now Frederick St), Ridge Av (now Bankridge Av), Meadow Av, Oak Tree Ter, Ramapo Av; Kinzie-Apgar basket factory by the Erie. Two parts.

sheet-3-2.description: The left part of sheet 3 lies west of the heavy line drawn along the New York and New Jersey state line and is turned on the page, with north pointing to the right, as its own north arrow shows. Most of it is in the Village of Suffern, New York, and is lettered 'This territory also shown on Suffern survey'. It shows a residential grid of State, 1st Street and Jersey Avenue running across the page and Brook Avenue, Ridge Avenue and Meadow Avenue at right angles to them, with Oak Tree Terrace at the top edge by the Ramapo River. The blocks are divided into numbered lots with frame dwellings and private garages; the state line runs as a dash-dot line through the blocks next to the heavy dividing line. At the bottom Ramapo Avenue runs towards the state line, and below it, beside the Erie Railroad main line tracks and Ramapo Valley Road, stands the Kinzie-Apgar & Son basket factory, with its warehouses and a note that it has no watchman, steam heat, electric light and steam and electric power. The large tracts at the left edge are left unsubdivided. The part continues the main part of the sheet across the state line, but because it is drawn at another rotation it is georeferenced separately.
notes: Turned on the page: north points to the right (fitted rotation about 75 degrees).
Brook Avenue is now Frederick Street; Ridge Avenue between 1st Street and Jersey Avenue is now Bankridge Avenue; Oak Tree Terrace is Oak Terrace; State is State Street.
The junction of Meadow Avenue and State Street lay about 15 m off a fit to the other points and was excluded.
Kinzie-Apgar & Son basket factory beside the Erie Railroad main line.
No control in the lower left (basket factory and Ramapo Valley Road); placement there is extrapolated from the street grid above it.

West village and the New York side at 100 ft. Part 1 (main, north up), right of the heavy line along the state line: Ramapo Valley Rd, Reich Av, 1st St (now Strysko Av), Franklin Av (now Franklin Pl), Hines, 2nd St (now South St), Wilmuth, Abelone (on the line of today's Sherwood Av), Warhol, Sherwood Av (on the line of today's Grove St), Island Rd, Avenue A, Avenue B, 1st St (now Church St), 2nd, 3rd Sts, Maple Av; First Zion Church. Part 2, left of the line, turned with north to the right: Village of Suffern, N.Y. ('This territory also shown on Suffern survey'): State, 1st St, Jersey Av, Brook Av (now Frederick St), Ridge Av (now Bankridge Av), Meadow Av, Oak Tree Ter, Ramapo Av; Kinzie-Apgar basket factory by the Erie. Two parts.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 shows the north end of Mahwah village near the New York state line, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with north at the top. Most of the sheet is taken up by the works of the American Brakeshoe & Foundry Company, which lie along the west side of the Erie Railroad main line: two long foundry buildings with core rooms, cleaning, shipping and tumbling rooms, sand and coke bins and scrap iron bins beside the sidings, a power house, an office, a pattern shop and pattern warehouse, a testing laboratory, an experimental foundry, a brakeshoe filling building and a locomotive house, with a note on the plant's watchman, heating, power and water supply drawn from the pond and a spring. Winters Brook runs south through the works from a pond fed by the Mahwah River, which crosses the top left of the sheet under Ramapo Valley Road. In the north-west corner small dwellings and shops line Reich Avenue and Shoe at the junction of Ramapo Valley Road. Along the west edge Island Road runs south past Warhol Street and Sherwood Avenue, with the Polish Roman Catholic church and a short unopened street of lots, and Kalura runs south from Ramapo Valley Road between Island Road and the brook. East of the railroad Franklin Turnpike runs the length of the sheet from Fox Lane at the top, with Christie Avenue and an unnamed street opening off it, a garage, a filling station and a few dwellings; the North Jersey Rapid Transit Company's electric right of way crosses the large open tracts at the east edge.
notes: Kalura (arbitrary name) is now North Railroad Avenue.
The street marked 'Not Named' off Franklin Turnpike is now Cedar Hill Avenue.
Shoe lies about where Brakeshoe Place now runs.
Fox Lane is drawn on both sides of Franklin Turnpike; today only the part east of the turnpike carries the name. The junction was hand-picked from the drawn edges.
The five-way junction of Reich Avenue, Ramapo Valley Road and Island Road was not detected; Ramapo Valley Road is drawn about 32 ft wide against a 61 to 73 ft modern right of way.
American Brakeshoe & Foundry Co. works, with a testing laboratory and an experimental foundry.

American Brakeshoe & Foundry Co. works at 100 ft, between Ramapo Valley Rd and Island Rd on the west and Franklin Turnpike on the east, Erie R.R. main line, Winters Brook, pond, Mahwah River; also Reich Av, Shoe, Kalura, Warhol St, Christie Av, Fox Lane, Polish R.C. Church. One part.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 shows the Craigmere residential tract south-east of the village centre, drawn at 150 ft to an inch rather than the 100 ft of the other sheets and turned on the page so that north points to the left. Miller Road runs down the left edge and Airmount Road down the right; Franklin Turnpike and the North Jersey Rapid Transit Company's trolley right of way cross the bottom. Between them Mahwah Road runs down the middle of the sheet, crossed by Beveridge Road, Alcott Road, Armour Road, Malcolm Road and Oweno Road, with Maysenger Road and a continuation of Mahwah Road to Franklin Turnpike in the lower part. At the top Mahwah Road turns east as a loop of streets around blocks of lots, with the Craigmere Water Works (an elevated water tank and a deep-well pump driven by a gasoline engine, 'for domestic services only') at the top edge. The letters of the name Craigmere are spread across the blocks. The tract is laid out in long rows of narrow numbered lots, most of them still vacant, with scattered frame dwellings, a few stuccoed and stone houses, private garages and a cobbler's shop. Other features are a pond in the block south of a curved street off Miller Road, a building of The Mahwah Co. with a hitching shed and store house, the fire department house on Hillside Avenue near Miller Road, and a short stretch of King Street (Franklin Lane) and Hillside Avenue at the lower left, which continue on sheet 2. Land east of Airmount Road above the lots is marked as woods. Large unsubdivided tracts lie outside the drawn lots at the left and top.
notes: Drawn at 150 ft to an inch, turned on the page with north to the left; the fitted scale (2.65 px/ft) agrees with the 100 ft sheets.
The unnamed loop streets at the top are now Highland Road and Summit Road, and the stretch of Mahwah Road south of Oweno Road is now South Mahwah Road.
The junctions of Oweno Road with Mahwah Road and with Miller Road lay 5 to 6 m off the fit and were excluded; Oweno Road west of Mahwah Road has been realigned.
Craigmere Water Works: elevated water tank and deep-well pump with gasoline engine, for domestic services only.
The Mahwah Co. building and the fire department house are on the Miller Road side of the tract.

Residential tract south of Miller Rd at 150 ft to an inch, turned on the page (north to the left): Miller Rd, Mahwah Rd, Beveridge Rd, Alcott Rd, Armour Rd, Malcolm Rd, Oweno Rd, Maysenger Rd, Airmount Rd, Hillside Av, King (Franklin Lane), Franklin Turnpike, N.J. R.T. Co. trolley right of way; Craigmere Water Works, fire department, 'The Mahwah' and a pond. One part.
